newsitem.title: FRANCE: French spy photos put query on US Iraq move - daily.
newsitem.headline: French spy photos put query on US Iraq move - daily.

text.p: Pictures taken by a French spy satellite have caused friction with Washington by casting doubt on whether Iraqi troop movements were big enough to justify U.S. missile raids, the French daily Le Monde said on Wednesday.

It said secret photographs taken by the new Helios satellite helped explain France's refusal to back Washington, its Gulf War ally, after this month's U.S. cruise missile attacks to punish an Iraqi attack on Kurds in northern Iraq.
Defence Ministry officials declined comment on the report.
France developed the Helios, with help from Spain and Italy, after the 1991 Gulf War to reduce its dependence on U.S. spying gear.

Le Monde said U.S. intelligence had reported major Iraqi troop movements in northern Iraq in August near the city of Erbil, citing pictures taken by reconnaissance flights and up to six spy satellites. It had stated that up to 40,000 soldiers were involved.

However, the Helios pictures "apparently did not detect such major movements of the Republican Guard in Iraqi Kurdistan," the daily said. "The French experts revised down the intelligence from American sources."
U.S. President Bill Clinton ordered the missile attacks against Iraq in retaliation for Baghdad's military offensive in support of one Kurdish faction against a rival rebel group in northern Iraq.
Le Monde said France had judged the strikes to be disproportionate retaliation by Washington and disapproved of "planned or systematic strikes" against Iraq.

The newspaper said pictures by Helios were not as good as data collected by U.S. spy satellites but "in military headquarters and intelligence services in France, the Helios is considered a thorn in the foot of the Americans."
